This results in the exact issue/inaccuracy I've mentioned in https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/14419#issuecomment-4038995795. E.g. after typing in the editor `116.0 / 156` you see in the editor `0.74` entered in. See the dicrepancy:
```gdscript
extends TileMapLayer

func _ready() -> void:
	print("%.25f" % [tile_set.flat_side_ratio])
	var value_double: float = 116.0 / 156 # GDScript `float` is 64-bit.
	tile_set.flat_side_ratio = value_double
	print("%.25f" % [tile_set.flat_side_ratio])
	print("%.25f" % [value_double])
```
```
0.7400000095367431640625000 // Entered in the editor.
0.7435897588729858398437500 // Double stored as float, without EditorSpinSlider rounding.
0.7435897435897436125173954 // Actual calculated double.
```

I don't think we should ship this when it's properly usable only from code (for ratios requiring more decimal places).
Then I guess the code should store `flat_side_ratio` instead, with the computation moved to _get_tile_overlap.

I may be a bit mistaken on this, but:
Having pixel values is also not ideal, imo. Hexagonal tiles are often anti-aliased and being able to put the the end of the flat side in in between two pixel can be more accurate. Pixel values are ints, meaning if they are used the flat side can end only on the beginning of a pixel. 
That being said, the value can be a float in the 0.0 to tile_size range.



Checked out how [https://thorbjorn.itch.io/tiled] implemented this feature, and they do have "Tile Side Length (Hex)" be an int value in pixels from 0 to tile_size. This is a bit less ergonomic when changing tile_size, but does allow for better precision for higher tile sized.  Just something for reference.

Can implement it this way if thats preferred. We need to make a decision on if a floating point or int px value to use. I think px values are fine for the most part, but for small tile sizes it might be a bit too coarse.

I don't think the inaccuracy is a big issue TBH, since there's no simple way to pixel-perfect align tiles in the float computations world under the hood, I think users should expect to have to add an additional pixel for precision.

My main issue with going with pixels is that we cannot provide a sensible default value, since it depends on the tile_size. So well, it means the hexagonal shape won't be usable out of the box. Also, it would need to be automatically clamped to the tile_size too, which is a bit annoying to track. 

Edit: also, it's kind of compat-breaking.

Or maybe... I have an idea! We could store the `flat_size_lenght` value internally as an integer offset from the `tile_size / 2` value.

So if `flat_size_lenght == tile_size / 2`, we store `0`, otherwise we store a negative value if it's smaller, and a positive value if it's longer. That way, the default value can stay 0 and, changing the tile_size should not impact the look of things with the default value.

I will call that value flat side length modifier.
Just to be sure before I start implementing this. I am thinking of dynamically setting the range to be in the "good range", that is all fine, but if a user sets the length modifier value super high, then scales the size down, the modified length might create the overlap value to be >0.5 or <0. At those values the tile selection is broken, and overall I think those values should be avoided, such that users dont see them.

TLDR: is it fine to clamp the flat side length modifier value when changing the size of the tile?

other than that I think its a robust solution

> I will call that value flat side length modifier.

I mean, this does not need to be exposed. You can expose a `flat_side_length` property that is not saved to disk but exposed in the inspector. Then this property simply updates an internal  `flat_side_length_modifier` that is not exposed but stored on disk.

>  TLDR: is it fine to clamp the flat side length modifier value when changing the size of the tile?

Hmm. I think I would avoid doing that. Instead, it can be clamped when using it instead. Having a property that depends on another kind of breaks undo/redo and can lead to unwanted file changes.

Visualization of the issue with the current implementation (click to expand)

Here's an example tile (120x23 size; 88 flat side length; one pixel black border on transparent background): -><- To make the borders of the neighboring tiles overlap you can set `TileSet.tile_size` to 118x22 and keep `TileSetAtlasSource.texture_region_size` as 120x23. Inaccuracy after setting `flat_side_ratio` to `88.0 / 118` in the editor is visible even for the `(0, 0)` cell: The same with neighbor cells added, see the pixel overlaps: | -|- After setting the same ratio in code (add script + reload the scene): ```gdscript @tool extends TileMapLayer func _ready() -> void: tile_set.flat_side_ratio = 88.0 / 118 ``` you can see no misalignment/overlaps: || -|-|-

As seen the potential unintentional micro gaps/overlaps can be avoided (or rather the error can be minimized), we should aim for that. --- > Having pixel values is also not ideal, imo. Hexagonal tiles are often anti-aliased and being able to put the the end of the flat side in in between two pixel can be more accurate. Pixel values are ints, meaning if they are used the flat side can end only on the beginning of a pixel. That being said, the value can be a float in the 0.0 to tile_size range. > Can implement it this way if thats preferred. We need to make a decision on if a floating point or int px value to use. I think px values are fine for the most part, but for small tile sizes it might be a bit too coarse. To be clear, I meant pixel units, it doesn't have to be `int`. Just changing the unit to pixels already improves the precision a lot. Editor truncating something like `0.005` from the ratio is a potentially big issue (as visualized above), truncating `0.005` from the pixel value is likely to be negligble / just fine. But also note that for a whole-pixels/integer input there should be no error introduced at all even when the property is `float`. So I think using `float` only makes it more customizable, there's no penalty for the integer cases. Personally I'm in favor of a `float` property in pixels. So if you have slight/uneven antialiasing or whatever on the tile borders then you could try tweaking it to subpixel/non-integer values. I don't see why would we need to limit the user here. Again, even for `float` property type the integer values would be storable without any error (tile sizes are not that big to reach float's integer precision). I guess if we really want to discourage subpixel values then the editor slider could have `step = 1.0`; but then subpixel values would be assignable only from the code. I'm not a fan of that but it would be an acceptable compromise to me. Also note that we can't pick `int` now and change later to `float` only if there's a demand from the users, this would be compatiblity breaking. Hence I'm in favor of using `float` straight away. > Or maybe... I have an idea! We could store the `flat_size_lenght` value internally as an integer offset from the `tile_size / 2` value. > > So if `flat_size_lenght == tile_size / 2`, we store `0`, otherwise we store a negative value if it's smaller, and a positive value if it's longer. That way, the default value can stay 0 and, changing the tile_size should not impact the look of things with the default value. Makes sense to me! I'm still in favor of using float though. 🙃
yeah ok, `flat_size_lenght` and the underlying property can be float, that's fine.

If we expose `flat_side_modifier` then it has a good property of default ui value always making the default regular hexagon.

> Wait quick question, are we exposing flat_side_length to the user?

`flat_side_length` is exposed to the user yes, but it should be stored on disk as the offset in pixel (called `flat_side_modifier`).

>  If so then yeah i just keep the overlap float value on the backend, to preserve the shape when changing the size. 

No, the problem with that approach is that it's less precise compared to a value in pixel. This, indeed, can be a problem for pixel-art games.

> If we expose `flat_side_modifier`

No, only `flat_side_length` is exposed as a "proxy" property. `flat_side_modifier` is what's stored on disk.

>  Personally i think flat_side_length being exposed is better as its super easy to understand and doesnt need extra explaining to the users. Just want to get a confirmation that we are fine with default value in the editor being a bit weird(probably being 8px which is super short for larger tiles).

The default value of `flat_side_length` will depend on the default value of `flat_side_modifier` (zero) and `tile_size`. `flat_side_length` should be computed as `tile_size / 2 + flat_side_modifier`, thus its default value should be `tile_size / 2`.
